title: Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl)
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this engine component application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by low-pressure turbine blade, gamma-tial intermetallic and service environment demands.
process: 5-axis CNC roughing for engine component geometry
Wire EDM contour profiling with SPC sampling
CMM per AS9102 with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for lowpressure turbine blade application
commonFailures: SCC in chloride-rich marine atmosphere - controlled by bake-out 300C + corrosion-inhibiting primer — critical for lowpressure turbine blade performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) suitable for Low-pressure turbine blade, gamma-TiAl intermetallic?
faq.a: Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address engine component operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl)?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for lowpressure turbine blade requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. lowpressure turbine blade components require Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for lowpressure turbine blade application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet lowpressure turbine blade specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
